reviews.rationale: There is no fixed prior-night-arrival habit. Erin explicitly resists unnecessary buffer nights, accepts same-day arrivals when the actual nonstop timing protects the first obligation, and adds a prior night when mandatory check-in, equipment, weather, or a thin arrival window makes same-day travel fragile. The proposed fact-based policy is supported.

Car choice tracks geography, equipment, parking, and trip purpose. Erin rents SUVs or crossovers for suburban multi-site work and family trips with gear, but explicitly rejects rentals for urban, conference-centered trips such as Orlando, Seattle, and Indianapolis. No general rental-car or SUV preference is supported.

Erin often accepts an amenity gap to avoid a burdensome work commute, but that is agenda- and gear-dependent rather than a universal closest-hotel rule. When the purpose changes to a spouse extension, recovery weekend, or convention experience, she selects resort, Warehouse District, waterfront, or other less work-adjacent locations. The proposed contextual ranking policy is appropriate.

The record rejects both an always-block and an always-independent rule. Erin uses blocks when early starts, badge pickup, teardown, or attached-event access materially reduce risk; she uses independent hotels when policy permits and rate, amenities, room quality, or weekend value are better. San Diego was even revised from independent to block work nights after the agenda changed.

A reusable soft preference is supported: Erin dislikes hotel moves on work trips and wants a material payoff before accepting one. She explicitly says she hates changing hotels unless the upside is real, later chooses continuous stays to avoid friction, and accepts splits only for substantial route, schedule, or confirmed leisure benefits. The proposed policy is operationally sensible but incomplete because it treats this durable anti-move baseline as merely trip-specific rather than retaining it as a soft preference.

Erin does not have a fixed next-day-return or same-day-return habit. She takes same-day evening flights when final timing is reliable, including late flights for a useful current-trip event, but extends when equipment, weather, a moved agenda, or airport-transfer math makes the same-day option brittle. The proposed return-risk policy matches the evidence.

Airport selection is based on door-to-door practicality, weather, equipment, route direction, holiday traffic, and total package cost. Erin pays for the more convenient airport in some cases, uses Albuquerque instead of Santa Fe when conditions support it, uses Eugene as a route-end airport, and applies explicit savings thresholds to Richmond, Chicago, and Milwaukee alternatives. No primary-airport default is justified.

Suite, fridge, desk, and work-base features become important when Erin is sorting shipments, storing cartons, handling equipment, or doing multi-site work. She nevertheless accepts standard block rooms or urban event hotels when conference access and schedule control dominate. The evidence supports evaluating those features from current operational needs rather than storing them as mandatory hotel preferences.
